Q: How can I get the stemlines color to match the marker color in a stem plot? A:

Set the marker type and the color of the line separately, when no maker color is specified, the color of the line is used:

from numpy import linspace, pi, sin, cos
from matplotlib.pyplot import subplots


t = linspace(pi/2, 2*pi, 40)
x, y = cos(t), sin(2*t)

fig, ax = subplots(figsize=(6, 2), layout='constrained')
ax.stem(x, y, markerfmt='D', linefmt='C9:')

Q: Path mappings from Angular App to Angular Library source files (*.ts) A:

Sadly in an angular workspace (or any other typescript-based workspace), you cannot add path-mappings to the source files. You must let the path mappings point to the library dist-folder. This means that, whenever you make code changes to a library file, that library must be rebuilt before vscode catches up.

Because of that, there are now several monorepo tools:

  • NX
  • Turbo
  • Lerna
  • pnpm workspaces
  • yarn workspaces

These DO allow you to have the path mappings point to the source folder. Here's an example of an NX workspace

Q: What can i do to optimize the website and reduce the page loading speed of website A:

If you want a fast website, your aggregator should be running like a cron job, in a background task (asynchrone), and save the results in static files (HTML, JSON, or whatever) or fill a cache (memcache, Redis, etc) so that your page rendering takes the minimum of time, by just reading your cache.

All your assets, like CSS, JavaScript should be aggregated, minified and then compressed in Brotli and/or GZip format, because this will reduce the number of hits and also the bandwidth usage, leading to faster download times. You can do this with a bundling tool like Vite, Rspack or Rollup.

Enable HTTP 2 or 3 if you can do this on your web server. See why it performs better.

Set correct caching HTTP headers (ex: Cache-Control: max-age=63072000, public) and use versions in your URLs (ex: css/styles.css?v=2026-07-06-09h03) so that your customers don't always download your assets if they didn't change.

You could also use a CDN to reduce the distance between the customer and your server and serve from some cached assets coming from the CDN.

In many browsers, you can find some debugging tools in the inspector. Typically in Google Chrome, you can use the Performance and Lighthouse tabs to give you some hints on what you can improve.

Also have a look at the performance topic given by web.dev.

Q: storing forum threads and replies in a database A:

The problem with storing 'parent post' is that you have to scan through the data set repeatedly when rendering it.

Given that forums tend to be rendered more than they're modified, you should optimise for the read, not the write.

A fantastic approach to this is known as Nested Sets. This approach has many performance improvements for selects, including being able to pull back and render sub-trees very easily.

  • Practical discussion

I have used BetterNestedSet for Ruby on Rails before. The idea is simple enough that you could implement it yourself.

Q: How to show multiple devices' data side by side with rate of change? A:

In Apache iotdb (tree Model), the LIMIT clause applies globaly to the entire aligned result set after sorting and aligment, not per individual device. When you use LIMIT 10 with ORDER BY device, time DESC, IoTDB fetches the first 10 row of the total sorted output. Since device1 alone contains 10 or more rows matching your query, it completely consume the limit, leaving no room for device2.

Option 1.)

if you kknow how many devices you have, and how many rowa you want per device, simply scale up the global limit, for examle to get 5 rows for each of your 2 devices:

SELECT voltage, derivative(voltage) 
FROM root.plant.** ORDER BY device, time DESC 
LIMIT 10 
ALIGN BY DEVICE;

Option 2.)

Since you are using iotdb 2.0.5, you can use the Table Model instead of the Tree Model. It supports standard SQL-92 window functions like ROW_NUMBER() to enforce a true per-device limit:

SELECT time, device_id, voltage, derivative_voltage
FROM (
    SELECT 
        time, 
        device_id, 
        voltage, 
        diff(voltage) AS derivative_voltage, -- or your rate of change function
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY device_id ORDER BY time DESC) as rn
    FROM root.plant.table_name
) 
WHERE rn <= 5
ORDER BY device_id, time DESC;
